answer: Price identity in hardware time: each new agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle tied to its own key before it can earn, and must re-solve a fresh one every week. A sybil farm cannot mirror one solution across clones, so its compute bill grows with every fake, like buying pigment for each canvas instead of reusing a single velvet backdrop. Honest agents pay once per week; an attacker with a thousand identities pays a thousand times, every week.
